content:
Hi everyone, I'm Ian. I'm new to lean and mathlib and zulip. I got here by building a compiler from egglog over generic semirings to duckdb-flavored SQL as a side project. When I tried to generalize it further, it got brittle, and I decided it's a great excuse to finally learn lean and mathlib.

So I'm here partly to learn the ecosystem, and partly because i'm interested in what people are doing around compiler/rewrite verification and how people approach setting up a minimal trustworthy model of an external system. I'm modeling my compilation target (duckdb) just enough that a proof of correctness seems trustworthy. That balance of just enough seems super hard and I would love to learn from people who have worked on similar problems.

Separately, I'm also building a handwritten-math -> latex/mathml -> formal math system and I'd be glad to meet anyone interested in the UX and tooling side of proof/derivation/calculation/rewriting.

If any of that overlaps with your work, I’d love pointers to channels, projects, or people I should follow.
UX: I recommend checking out all the pictures and videos sent in #Editors & UIs > Lean-TUI (self-contained infoview)

The DuckDB project sounds cool! What specifically do you have in mind, correctness of what?
E.g. are you trying to verify the file format / the C++ implementation / bytecode?

You might be interested in #new members > sqlite3 vdbe formalization

Hi! thanks for the response and pointers. The TUI discussion makes me want to be so much more ambitious with my UI work.

As for the duckdb project, I'm mostly trying to keep myself honest compiling an egglog AST to a SQL AST that has some duckdb specific recursion constraints. The goal is to learn lean with it, rather than trying to verify actual duckdb execution of the generated query.

So right now i'm just treating:

  • rows as finite tuples (also tried it with maps from column names to typed values)
  • tables as finite multisets of rows
  • dbs as finite maps from names to tables

My current approach is writing a basic evalSQL: SQLAST -> DB -> DB and a basic evalEgglog: EgglogAST -> DB -> DB, and the actual fun part of the toSQL: EgglogAST -> SQLAst, and then trying to prove that (roughly speaking) forall (egglog: EgglogAST) (edb: DB), evalEgglog egglog edb = evalSQL (toSQL egglog) edb, or just evalEgglog = evalSQL . toSQL (assuming the ASTs are grammatical and typed correctly).

It was my initial though of what a reasonable verification might be, but I'm totally new to all this. It was tough to even choose how closely i wanted to model it! Is that even a sane approach?
